hook: You're not unfocused. You haven't moved in three hours — and your brain blood flow shows it.
topic: Sedentary behaviour, cerebral blood flow, and acute movement as a cognitive tool
body:
**Prolonged sitting measurably reduces blood flow to the prefrontal cortex. That is the part of your brain responsible for focus, decision-making, and the kind of clear linear thinking that complex work demands.**

This is not a metaphor. Cerebral blood flow in the prefrontal region begins declining after extended sedentary periods. The result is exactly what you feel: a progressive dimming of the capacity to hold complex thoughts, make rapid decisions, or sustain attention on a hard problem.

This is also why your thinking often improves on a walk. Not because walking is calming — though it is — but because movement acutely increases cerebral blood flow. The thinking gets better because the blood is getting there.

The implication is direct. If your cognitive performance is declining across a work session, the intervention is not more coffee, more discipline, or a harder deadline. It is five minutes of movement. Now.

Not because it is healthy in some general sense. Because it restores the physical substrate that thinking requires.
